theme: Geocoding, neighbourhood boundaries and census-tract crosswalks used for STR studies; city GIS portals with STR layers
queries_run: gh search repos "neighborhood boundaries geojson" --sort stars
gh search repos "census tract crosswalk" --sort stars
gh search repos "airbnb neighbourhoods geojson" --sort stars
gh search repos "city GIS short term rental" --sort stars
gh search repos "short term rental zoning" --sort stars
gh search repos "HUD USPS crosswalk" --sort stars
gh search repos "socrata open data discovery" --sort stars

candidates.name: mashvisor/us-neighborhoods-boundaries
candidates.what_it_holds: GeoJSON/CSV neighborhood-boundary shapefiles derived from Zillow's discontinued Neighborhood Boundaries dataset, covering 42 US states; committed conversion output, CC0 licence.
candidates.why_useful: US neighbourhood polygons are the join layer needed to aggregate Inside Airbnb listing lat/lon or STR registry addresses up to a consistent geography for cross-city comparison; Zillow's original file is no longer distributed so this mirror has standalone value.

candidates.name: AlexMotz/us-neighborhood-geojson
candidates.what_it_holds: US neighborhood polygons in GeoJSON, converted from the same open-sourced Zillow Neighborhood Boundaries shapefiles.
candidates.why_useful: Second independent mirror of the Zillow neighbourhood boundary geometry in a directly-loadable GeoJSON format for joining STR listing coordinates to neighbourhoods.

candidates.name: coddingtonbear/django-neighborhoods
candidates.what_it_holds: Django app + management commands importing Zillow neighborhood boundary data for most major US cities, plus a City-of-Portland-specific boundary loader; ships as importable fixtures/loaders rather than raw files only.
candidates.why_useful: A ready-made import/geocoding pipeline for turning point coordinates (Inside Airbnb listings, STR registry addresses) into neighbourhood names across many US metros at once.

candidates.name: staeco/neighborhood-boundaries
candidates.what_it_holds: Small MIT-licensed script that downloads and converts Zillow neighborhood boundary shapefiles to GeoJSON on demand.
candidates.why_useful: One-command puller for the same Zillow neighbourhood geometry other repos mirror statically; useful if the canonical Zillow source URL still resolves.

candidates.name: chriswhong/nyc-neighborhood-boundaries
candidates.what_it_holds: Single GeoJSON file of contiguous, non-overlapping polygons for New York City neighbourhoods (hand-corrected from NYC Planning's NTAs), committed to the repo.
candidates.why_useful: NYC is our largest single Inside Airbnb market and has the pre/post-Local-Law-18 gap (CONTEXT gap 1); a clean contiguous neighbourhood layer supports any tract-level rollup of NYC listings/registrations.

candidates.name: tsdataclinic/newerhoods
candidates.what_it_holds: NYC Data Clinic project aggregating NYC Open Data at the census-tract level and using ML (clustering) to redraw data-driven neighbourhood boundaries; includes tract-level feature tables and boundary-generation code, Apache-2.0.
candidates.why_useful: Provides both a census-tract-level NYC dataset and a method for building STR-relevant neighbourhood definitions from tract data, useful for any tract-to-neighbourhood crosswalk work on NYC STR data.

candidates.name: DNAinfoData/Draw-Your-Neighborhood
candidates.what_it_holds: Crowdsourced neighbourhood boundary polygons for New York City and Chicago, collected by DNAinfo's mapping project; GPL-3.0.
candidates.why_useful: Independent, resident-drawn neighbourhood polygons for two of our 13 core Inside Airbnb cities (NYC, Chicago), an alternative to official planning-department boundaries for STR listing aggregation.

candidates.name: CT-Data-Collaborative/2022-tract-crosswalk
candidates.what_it_holds: 2010-vintage census tract crosswalk file mapping Connecticut tracts to town, county, county-equivalent, ZIP code and PUMA.
candidates.why_useful: Template/example of a state-level tract-to-place crosswalk; useful as a pattern for building similar tract-to-city crosswalks for other STR markets, though state coverage (CT) is narrow for ABNB purposes.

candidates.name: hantswilliams/hud_usps_crosswalk_files
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed copies of HUD-USPS ZIP-code crosswalk files (ZIP to census tract / county / CBSA), which HUD otherwise only distributes as a paid/registration-gated quarterly download.
candidates.why_useful: A free mirror of the standard ZIP<->tract/county/CBSA crosswalk used to join STR registry data (often ZIP-level) to census geographies for regional aggregation; generally useful infrastructure for any of our municipal STR registry work.

candidates.name: alperen-acikol/hud-crosswalk
candidates.what_it_holds: Python toolkit wrapping the HUD USPS Crosswalk API to map survey ZIP codes to county FIPS codes; a client/method rather than a stored dataset.
candidates.why_useful: One-command puller for ZIP-to-county FIPS mapping, a lighter-weight alternative to hosting the static crosswalk files, for regional-aggregation work on ZIP-level STR/registry data.

notes: This theme is thin on GitHub: most "neighbourhood boundary" repos are either static Zillow-derived US shapefile mirrors (all deriving from the same discontinued Zillow ZNTA dataset, so heavily duplicative of each other) or single-city crowdsourced/planning-department polygon sets with no STR-specific content. Nothing found is Airbnb-specific or an STR-tagged city GIS portal layer per se -- city STR registries themselves (Austin, Barcelona HUTB, Maui, NYC OSE, CA TOT) are already held per CONTEXT.md and were excluded here as duplicates; searches for those turned up no GitHub mirrors beyond what's already catalogued. "city GIS short term rental layer" and "airbnb neighbourhoods geojson" queries returned zero results -- city GIS STR layers (e.g. LA HSO, SF OSTR map layers) do not appear to have GitHub mirrors distinct from the municipal open-data portals we already query directly. Socrata/CKAN open-data discovery client search also returned zero -- worth a differently-worded pass by another scout (try "socrata client", "ckan client python", "opendata scraper" as separate single-word-anchored queries) since CONTEXT gap #17 explicitly wants this. Did not find any academic replication package specifically building STR census-tract crosswalks; a scout with WebSearch budget could try Google Scholar / OSF for STR geocoding papers with committed code, which gh search cannot surface well. HUD-USPS crosswalk mirrors are the most concretely useful find here since HUD's own distribution requires registration.
